newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian lawmakers block extradition legislation.
newsitem.headline: Colombian lawmakers block extradition legislation.

text.p: A key congressional committee on Wednesday failed to approve the Colombian government's call for an end to the country's ban on extradition, ruling out any chance that it will be lifted this year.

After two days of heated debate, a constitutional committee of the Senate voted 8-8 against approving draft legislation that would lift the ban on extradition, imposed by Colombia's constituent assembly in 1991.

Constitutional reforms have to be approved by two consecutive sessions of Congress and the current session ends on June 20. For that reason, and because of opposition to the bill among many lawmakers, Wednesday's vote virtually ruled out any chance of the ban being lifted this year.
"The bill has sunk," said Sen. Luis Guillermo Giraldo, a leading proponent of seeing Colombia's drug lords and other criminals tried in the United States and other countries.
"This is a defeat for the whole country," he added, saying the vote would add to Colombia's drug-tarnished image abroad and meant "becoming even more isolated from the international community."

The government of President Ernesto Samper proposed the bill to restore extradition on April 29 under intense pressure from Washington. The United States has "decertified" Colombia for its anti-drug efforts for the past two years and argues that detention in a secure prison facility in the United States is what Colombia's powerful drug lords fear the most.
